correctness.rationale: Direct proof of the precise positive-parameter theorem in RESULT.md: coin length from parity and capacity, lambda(x+q)=lambda(x)+1, lambda(x+2j)>=lambda(x), lambda(x+a)>=lambda(x) for a>q, explicit Apéry representatives of Q=S/p, strict increase along each parity of r, and exact terminal/penultimate comparison. All assumptions and m=2 boundary are handled. Standalone Dijkstra graph computes Apéry residues without relying on this formula and matches 125586 valid cases, including 29598 positive corrections. The symbolic proof, not the finite experiment, justifies infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2023 primary full text supplies the Apéry computation but explicitly gives a Frobenius closed form only for even terminal remainder and calls odd remainder difficult. This finding provides the missing universal terminal/penultimate maximum and exact indicator correction, which is not stated by the checked 2018, 2023, 2026 papers or accessible indexed records. Its proof adds parity-class monotonicity and a branch evaluation, rather than claiming the existing Apéry formula is new. The original 2023 Apéry formula computes the answer by an O(a/p) maximum, so novelty is limited to the uniform closed maximum. Risks: 2025 journal full text uninspected; possible unindexed equivalents.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating primary paper explicitly leaves the odd terminal remainder closed Frobenius evaluation unresolved even though it derives every quotient Apéry element. The exact single-correction formula solves that motivated subproblem over an unbounded parameter family; the correction can grow without bound, and the two-step parity monotonicity gives a structural explanation rather than a mere numerical optimization exercise. No generic or downstream theorem is claimed; the precise natural quotient invariant has a clear use.
